=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tstart "_###_##_#_#_#_#__#__"
text tgen "generation "
text tcolon ": "
global cur uchar 20
global nxt uchar 20
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emitb writes the single byte c
fn emitb c ulong to void
d = new uchar 1 0
put d 0 uchar c
emit d
end
note a cell is alive next generation when exactly two of itself and its two neighbours are alive
note (cells beyond the ends are dead); the run stops when a generation repeats the one before
fn cell i ulong to ulong
if eq get cur i 35
ret 1
end
ret 0
end
fn step to bool
changed = false
for i ulong 20
n = cell i
if gt i 0
n = add n cell sub i 1
end
if lt i 19
n = add n cell add i 1
end
v = uchar 95
if eq n 2
v = 35
end
if ne v get cur i
changed = true
end
put nxt i v
end
for i ulong 20
put cur i get nxt i
end
ret changed
end
note 20 cells can change at most 2^20 ways, but this start settles after 9 generations; 100 is ample
fn main to int
for i ulong 20
put cur i get tstart i
end
g = ulong 0
while true bound 100
emit tgen
emitu g
emit tcolon
for i ulong 20
emitb ulong get cur i
end
emit nl
if not step
break
end
g = add g 1
end
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>

generation 2: __##___##_#_#_______

generation 4: __##___#_##_________
generation 5: __##____###_________
generation 6: __##____#_#_________
generation 7: __##_____#__________
